function.name: calculate_velocity
function.description: Calculate the final velocity of an object in motion given its initial velocity, acceleration and time. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity of the object in m/s. This is a float type value.

acceleration.description: The acceleration of the object in m/s^2. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time for which the object is in motion in seconds. This is a float type value.

message.content: I don’t have access to live data, so I can’t pull up a current list of releases from this moment. If you let me know what kind of movies you’re interested in—genre, country, release window (e.g., last week, last month), or even a particular platform—I can suggest some titles that were recently coming out around that time.
message.reasoning: User asks "What are the latest movie releases?" We need to respond with a list of recent movies. But we have no browsing capability. We can provide general info or ask clarifying question. According to policy, we cannot hallucinate. So we should ask for clarification: maybe user wants a list of movies released recently. We could say we don't have real-time data. Ask if they want specific genre or region.
